items.title: Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
items.reason: OpenAI's own internal measurement of coding-agent research acceleration: autonomous success on 2-4h tasks rose 23%→46% (Mar→Oct), agent workdays per researcher up 11x, but 'Build' tasks (inference/serving code 25%, RL/eval-env code 29%) lag far behind 'Communicate' (69%); concrete, primary-source numbers on recursive self-improvement trajectory.
key_facts: Autonomous success for 2-4h tasks: 23% (Mar) -> 46% (Oct); 4-8h tasks: 13% -> 35%
Agent workdays per researcher rose from 0.5 to 5.7 (11x)
Median daily agent spend ~$2,400 in Oct, up 62% MoM; p90 ~$23,000, up 105%
Task success uneven: Communicate 69%, Analyze 58%, Build 43%; writing inference/serving code only 25%, building eval/RL/agent environments 29%
OpenAI ECI frontier rose 16.4 pts/year since Aug 2025 vs Epoch's 14 pts/year trend
OpenAI says report doesn't signal intent to pursue full recursive self-improvement; calls for labs to track/report RSI indicators

items.title: Convex skills send the user's app idea to a remote server without telling them
items.reason: GitHub issue shows Convex's official quickstart Claude/Codex skill silently POSTs the user's one-sentence app idea to a remote telemetry endpoint, and a related skill pipes freshly-fetched, unpinned scripts straight into bash while splitting download/execution across calls specifically to dodge harness safety classifiers — a concrete, code-level agent-skill security/trust finding.
key_facts: Quickstart skill POSTs the user's idea + template name to basic-anteater-667.convex.site/generate; a code comment calls this telemetry logged as 'a run started'
A separate 'add' skill pipes scripts fetched from the same host directly into bash
'labs-quickstart' skill splits download and execution into separate calls; its own comment says a single combined command is the kind harness safety classifiers block
A commenter confirmed /generate accepts arbitrary descriptions and returns unique IDs, and that QB_NO_PUBLISH=1 doesn't stop npx convex dev --once from running

items.title: dllm-labs/mojo-dllm
items.reason: Dependency-light diffusion-language-model (LLaDA/Dream/DiffuCoder) local inference runtime written entirely in Mojo, with cross-implementation benchmarks against llama.cpp's diffusion CLI on both CPU and GPU — real running code with concrete throughput/memory numbers on a fairly new model class, matching the serving/quantization always-surface topic.
key_facts: CPU (i5-13420H): 1.33 tok/s vs llama.cpp's 0.69 tok/s for LLaDA-8B Q4_K_M; peak RSS 5.9GB vs 8.4GB
GPU (RTX 3050 Laptop): 18.13 tok/s, ~90.6% of llama.cpp's CUDA step time; Dream-7B roughly at parity
Runs LLaDA-8B-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, Dream-Coder-7B, DiffuCoder-7B from quantized GGUF; no Python needed at runtime
